sonnet.problem: The blank asks the baker to supply the Bible's own word 'Pit'. Nothing earlier in the walkthrough has introduced it, so 'Flood' or 'Wilderness' are equally reasonable guesses. This is wording the baker has not seen, not meaning they can reason out.
sonnet.rule: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

sonnet.problem: Card 13 already showed 'He earned his own healing' as a wrong answer. Card 14 then asks the same idea, whether the man takes credit for saving himself. The earlier answer is reused.
sonnet.rule: An answer shown on one card, right or wrong, isn't used again on a later card.

sonnet.problem: The question says Elihu 'wants Job to trust' his words. Verse 3 gives no reason or motive for why Elihu says this, so the card adds one.
sonnet.rule: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.
